findings.claim: npm test now implicitly downloads an engine on Linux CI. Provision the pinned Linux engine explicitly, or bundle it, instead of hiding installation inside the test.
findings.failureScenario: On a fresh ubuntu-latest runner, unavailable release assets or blocked GitHub release downloads make the launcher exit 127, failing npm test and blocking website publication.
findings.evidence: scripts/bin contains only darwin-arm64/impeccable. The launcher falls back to downloading engine-v0.1.14 and its checksum. .github/workflows/publish.yml runs npm ci then npm test without engine provisioning; npm dependencies do not supply that binary.

verification.evidence: Parent confirmed VERSION, bundled inventory, checksum validation and fail-closed exit 127. This is the vendor's intended first-run provisioning, not a test bypass. Documented network/cache requirements and explicit engine-probe/preinstalled-engine options in docs/publishing.md. Separate CI installation would move, not remove, the same network dependency. No Linux execution claimed.
